text:
Alex: CI red on PR #5698 — image promotion failed after merge. Build job `integration-image-build` failed in promotion step, logs say promoted tag not found.
ci-bot: job 42 build step failed: error: manifest for org/internal/app:pr-5698 not found
Alex: I refactored the Dockerfile (multi-stage) yesterday to reorder stages and removed an intermediate LABEL. Could that change the final manifest/digest? Here's the relevant diff snippet:
```Dockerfile
FROM rust:1.68 as builder
# ... build steps ...
FROM debian:bookworm as runtime
COPY --from=builder /app /app
LABEL maintainer="infra-team"
``` 
Maya: tag-mismatch errors often come from cache differences or from the CI using a different builder/platform. Did you change any labels or platform args? Also which registry (harbor/internal)?
Alex: Harbor (internal). I removed an unnecessary LABEL from the builder stage, not the runtime. Locally `docker build -t org/internal/app:pr-5698 .` succeeds and `docker inspect org/internal/app:pr-5698` shows RepoDigests: `org/internal/app@sha256:abcd1234`.
Sasha: registry can reject pushes if mediaType/annotations differ between manifest lists. BuildKit sometimes rewrites manifests. Also if CI builds for a different platform you'll get another digest.
Ravi: can you paste the CI error lines around the push/promotion step? Also what's the token-scoped permission for CI on harbor?
ci-bot: promotion-step: PUT /v2/org/internal/app/manifests/pr-5698 -> 403 Forbidden (error: insufficient scope: pushing to repo)
Alex: Hmm 403 during PUT suggests auth issue. But earlier it said manifest not found for pull. Maybe two separate problems: CI cache produced a different digest and promotion failed due to token scope.
Maya: quick triage:
- rerun CI build with `--no-cache --pull` to avoid cached layers
- ensure build uses same platform flags as local build (e.g., `--platform linux/amd64`)
- have CI promo step push by digest not tag (use `docker push org/internal/app@sha256:...`)
Alex: starting a local sanity run: `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build --no-cache --pull --platform linux/amd64 -t org/internal/app:pr-5698 .`
Sasha: also check if CI's builder is using BuildKit v0.11 vs local v0.12 — we had a parity issue before where OCI annotations changed.
Alex: local build produced digest `sha256:abcd1234` again. I'll trigger CI rerun now and attach logs.
ci-bot: rerun requested by Alex: integration-image-build #42 -> queued
Ravi: if rerun still fails, bisect the Dockerfile commits in the PR to find the exact change that led to different manifests. In the meantime, you can push by digest to promote.
Alex: CI rerun finished: build succeeded, but promotion still failed with 403 (token issue). Promotion step tries to PUT manifest for tag `pr-5698`.
Sasha: 403 is definitely auth. Can you check the CI secrets for registry write scope? We rotated the token last week for the runner.
Alex: confirmed the CI token is scoped to read/pull only. That explains 403. Strange that earlier run attempted push though.
Ravi: quick fix applied: I promoted the image by digest from my machine: `docker pull org/internal/app@sha256:abcd1234 && docker tag org/internal/app@sha256:abcd1234 org/internal/app:pr-5698 && docker push org/internal/app:pr-5698` (using a user token with push permissions). Service tests are green now.
Maya: follow-ups: (1) update promotion job to prefer digest-based promotion, (2) change CI token to include push only for promotion runner or use a separate promotion service account, (3) add `--no-cache` for suspect PR builds and pin BuildKit version in CI image.
Alex: opened infra ticket #242 to track CI promotion auth and changed promo to digest-based as a short-term fix. Also added `--no-cache` temporarily for this workflow. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Sasha: I'll add a note in the registry runbook about token scopes and promotion-by-digest.
Ravi: +1. If anyone sees similar flakiness, ping me and I'll help bisect.
Alex: awesome — triage complete, will close PR once infra changes land. Thanks all.
